title: Optimization of TiO2/SiO2/Glass High-Low Antireflection Stack
scientific_hypothesis: A two-layer stack with the higher-index material (TiO2, n=2.40) adjacent to the glass substrate (n=1.52) and the lower-index material (SiO2, n=1.46) facing air will provide a smoother effective index transition than the reverse order, potentially yielding a lower mean reflectance across the visible spectrum when thicknesses are optimized.
design_principle: Stepped refractive index matching: Air (1.0) -> Low (1.46) -> High (2.40) -> Substrate (1.52). This attempts to bridge the large index gap between air and the intermediate/high layers before reaching the substrate.
soft_objectives: Minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (s-pol, normal incidence) from 450 nm to 700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: Layer thicknesses strictly bounded between 40 nm and 160 nm
Exactly one layer of each material
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
Quarter-wave transformer approximation as an initial guess heuristic
expected_advantages: The high-index layer next to the glass may reduce the reflection coefficient at the second interface compared to a direct SiO2-Glass interface.
Two degrees of freedom (thicknesses) allow tuning for broadband performance.
known_risks: The index step from SiO2 (1.46) to TiO2 (2.40) is large and may cause significant internal reflection if not perfectly tuned.
Thickness constraints (40-160 nm) may prevent reaching the theoretical global minimum if it lies outside this box.
Two layers may be insufficient to achieve the <0.03 target over such a wide bandwidth.
execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic TMM optimization for a planar three-medium stack: Incident Air (n=1.0), Layer 1 (SiO2, n=1.46, lossless), Layer 2 (TiO2, n=2.40, lossless), Substrate Glass (n=1.52, lossless). Optimize the thickness of Layer 1 and Layer 2 to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence over the wavelength range 450 nm to 700 nm (5 nm spacing). Constraints: Thickness of Layer 1 in [40, 160] nm; Thickness of Layer 2 in [40, 160] nm. Use seed 17 for the optimizer. Maximum 64 solver evaluations. Report the optimal thicknesses, the full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm; achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450 nm to 700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.
